school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented study settings across NC State’s D. H. Hill Jr. and James B. Hunt Jr. Libraries, spanning silent reading rooms, collaborative areas, and computer-equipped commons.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Settle into a no-talking room with large reading tables and controllable lighting; enter through the gap between the second-floor study-room blocks.
cards.short_summary: A silent, light-filled reading room with large tables.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes the Hunt Quiet Reading Room as a tranquil, light-filled study and reflection space with large tables and a no-talking sound level.
cards.source_title: Quiet Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, second floor; the library directs visitors through the library gates and past the elevator bay. Check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Skyline Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fifth Floor
cards.notes: Use the fifth-floor tables, soft seating, and standing-height table when you want a silent setting with natural light and Lake Raleigh-facing views.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-floor silent room with natural light and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries states that the Skyline Reading Room has reading tables, soft seating, abundant natural light, views, and a no-talking sound level.
cards.source_title: Skyline Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fifth floor. Check current library hours and building access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Oval View Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Bring an individual task to the fourth-floor room, which combines lounge seats, work tables, natural light, and a hushed-voices setting overlooking the Oval.
cards.short_summary: Hushed fourth-floor seating overlooking the Oval.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries documents lounge seating, work tables, natural light, hushed voices, and views over Hunt Library and the Centennial Campus Oval.
cards.source_title: Oval View Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fourth floor; the library provides elevator and stair directions from the entrance. Check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Lake Raleigh Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Choose a computer workstation or collaborative table in this fourth-floor commons, where three walls of windows bring in daylight and Lake Raleigh views.
cards.short_summary: A computer-equipped commons with three-sided floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes computer workstations for individual and collaborative work, colorful furniture, floor-to-ceiling windows on three sides, and Lake Raleigh views.
cards.source_title: Lake Raleigh Learning Commons, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fourth floor. The listed equipment includes Mac, Windows, and Linux Engineering desktops; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Idea Alcove
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor · Room 2302
cards.notes: Use the movable furniture and wall-sized whiteboard for an impromptu working session near the Quiet Reading Room; keep voices appropriate for an active space.
cards.short_summary: An informal collaboration area with mobile furniture and a full-wall whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries identifies the Idea Alcove as an open, informal collaboration space with movable furniture, large tables, lockers, and a whiteboard covering the north wall.
cards.source_title: Idea Alcove, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, second floor, Room 2302, near the Quiet Reading Room. This space is listed with conversation-and-chatter sound level; check current library hours.

cards.title: Study Room 3315
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-person room for a focused group session; it has a work table, whiteboard, controllable white-noise speaker, and overlooks the Quiet Reading Room.
cards.short_summary: A reservable six-person group room overlooking the Quiet Reading Room.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists Study Room 3315 as a six-person room with a work table, whiteboard, controllable white-noise speaker, and student/faculty/staff reservations up to seven days ahead.
cards.source_title: Study Room 3315, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, third floor. Reservable up to seven days in advance for up to two hours by students, graduate students, faculty, and staff; a 15-minute arrival grace period applies.

cards.title: Hill Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · First Floor, West Wing · Rooms 1325 and 1311
cards.notes: For individual silent work, use the glass-walled room’s work tables and picture-window views toward the terrace and Brickyard; no talking is permitted.
cards.short_summary: A glass-separated silent room with Brickyard-facing windows.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes Hill’s Quiet Reading Room as individual silent-study space, isolated from ambient noise by a glass wall, with work tables and no talking.
cards.source_title: Quiet Reading Room, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, first floor West Wing, Rooms 1325 and 1311. The library provides routes from Brickyard and Hillsborough Street entrances; check current hours.

cards.title: Ground Floor Reading Room
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Ground Floor, Tower
cards.notes: Spread out at a large table or choose lounge seating in this traditional library-style reading room; the circulating DVD collection is also housed here.
cards.short_summary: A large traditional reading room with tables and lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries calls the Ground Floor Reading Room a large study space with traditional library-style seating, lounge seating, and large tables.
cards.source_title: Ground Floor Reading Room, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, ground-floor Tower. Check current library hours and access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: North Forum
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Third Floor, Tower
cards.notes: Set up a collaborative session at the configurable large work tables and whiteboards just north of the Visualization Studio; this is a conversation-and-chatter area.
cards.short_summary: An open third-floor work area with configurable tables and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes the North Forum as an open study area north of the Visualization Studio with large configurable work tables and whiteboards.
cards.source_title: North Forum, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, third-floor Tower, north of the Visualization Studio. Listed sound level is conversation and chatter; check current library hours.

cards.title: Study Lounge 2301
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Second Floor, West Wing · Room 2301
cards.notes: Take a casual study break at a booth or table in this naturally lit lounge, which also has a whiteboard and nearby food and drink vending machines.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit lounge with booth seating, tables, and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists Study Lounge 2301 as a study space with casual booth seating, tables and chairs, natural light, a whiteboard, and vending machines.
cards.source_title: Study Lounge 2301, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, second-floor West Wing, Room 2301. The library provides routes from the Brickyard entrance; check current library hours before visiting.
